rows.label: PGQ-006, draft 1 of 2 (not in: failed alone twice; your answers needed)
rows.text: Your own history with psychedelics and other drugs counts here too, more than anybody's trip report. Say something once gave you a psychotic kind of reaction, like voices or paranoia. It's easy to chalk that up to a bad night or a bad batch, especially if you've felt totally fine since. I still wouldn't take it again without a professional assessment. Same if you kept seeing things after it should've worn off. A reaction like that says something about how your own mind handles those states, so I'd be careful with anything else that messes with your sense of what's real, too. Not every drug, though.
rows.after_row: P2, new: why not just blast past it (your San Pedro line)
source: Your own track record with psychoactive substances matters.
notes: Your queue item: "one prior psychotic-type reaction or persisting perceptual reaction is enough to gate retesting that same substance pending professional assessment ... this is not a blanket anti-drug rule".

Question 1: does paranoia during a rough trip count as the one episode, or only a psychotic-type reaction, beyond what that drug usually does? The guide's "persists beyond the expected intoxication" qualifies only the visuals, so as written it reads like any paranoid trip counts.
Question 2: which other drugs would you name as the ones that "mess with your sense of what's real" (cannabis? ketamine? MDMA?). The guide names none, and a reader may not think of theirs as one.
Pangram alone: 100% AI (111; try 1 without "a bad night or a bad batch"), then 100% AI (113).

rows.label: PGQ-006, draft 2 of 2 (not in)
rows.text: Milder reactions count too, like getting confused or spaced out again and again (not the fun kind of spaced out). If one of these reactions ever gets severe, or you can't tell whether you're safe, get professional help right away. If it keeps coming back when you're sober, even mildly, get it looked at too. And if you start to wonder whether a prescription, or anything your body's come to depend on, is part of the problem, the obvious move is to just quit it. Please don't, though, or not cold turkey anyway. Coming off some things too fast is its own danger, and a doctor can help you taper.
rows.after_row: PGQ-006, draft 1 of 2 (not in: failed alone twice; your answers needed)
source: Your own track record with psychoactive substances matters.
notes: The rest of the item: milder reactions, professional help (now, and for sober recurrence even when mild), and never stopping a prescription or anything your body depends on cold.
Pangram alone: 58% AI (106; its second half, the medication part), then 100% AI (115). If you'd rather, I can fold the core of both drafts into one sentence of P2 once you've answered.
